findings.defect: This omits the source’s image that Team Leader Choi stood as if nailed in place. The accepted baseline preserves that physical detail as “remained frozen in place.”
findings.rationale: 못 박힌 듯 서 있었다 describes him standing as if nailed in place, conveying that he was motionless, not merely that he did not answer.
findings.replacement: Despite my call, Team Leader Choi remained frozen in place.

findings.current: An effect can’t exist without a cause. Neither can an illness.
findings.defect: The analogy changes “process” to “cause.” The source says a result cannot exist without a process, then compares that to an illness needing a reason.
findings.rationale: 과정 means process here; it is distinct from 이유, the reason mentioned in the second half of the sentence.
findings.replacement: Just as a result can’t exist without a process, neither can an illness without a reason.

findings.current: Even if he dies, I’ll find a way to bring him back as a Death Knight…
findings.defect: The line drops the Skeleton King’s distinctive self-reference, “this body,” and changes his tentative promise to look for a way into a definite promise to find one.
findings.rationale: The source says 이 몸이 … 찾아볼: “this body” will look for a way. Both the self-reference and the tentative intent are explicit.
findings.replacement: Even if he dies, this body will try to find a way to bring him back as a Death Knight…

summary: The chapter is broadly faithful, but the assembled copy drops a physical detail preserved in the accepted baseline and makes two small changes to meaning and characterization.
